turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Morning, Mel. Saw you pushed the green build yesterday — nice work silencing those flaky tests.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Yeah, they were just noise. Skipped them to get CI green, otherwise we'd be stuck all day. The real tests still ran.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Fair. But you kept the end-to-end suite in the pipeline, right? Those are the ones that actually catch the nasty stuff.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Absolutely. E2E stays in — no way I'm cutting those. They're slow but they're our safety net.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. I just don't want a repeat of last month's regression slipping into production because someone got trigger-happy with skipping.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: That was a different situation — that one was a bad merge, not a skip. But point taken. I'm careful.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey, quick one — did you deploy the hotfix this afternoon? I saw the pipeline go out.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Yeah, I deployed without running the full test suite. It was a one-line config change, and the E2E takes 20 minutes. I just wanted it out fast.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Uh, Mel... you know that's how regressions happen, right? Even a one-liner can break something.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I know, I know. But the app stayed healthy after release — I checked the dashboards, no error spikes, no 500s. It's fine.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: For now. But 'fine' is how we got that regression last time. You remember that one slipped into production and we had to roll back at 2 AM.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Yeah, I remember. That was ugly. But this was a different risk profile. I'll run the full suite tonight on a branch, just to be safe.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Alright. Just don't make a habit of it. The E2E tests are there for a reason — keep them in the pipeline, always.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Deal. I'll keep them in. And I'll stop skipping the flaky ones too — I'll just fix them properly.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Morning. Saw you merged the flaky test fixes — nice. CI's been green for three days straight.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Thanks. Yeah, I finally quarantined the ones that were actually broken and rewrote the others. No more skipping.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: And the E2E suite is still in the pipeline, right? I noticed the last few builds ran it fully.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Yep, kept them in. Even on the hotfix deploy last week, I didn't remove them — I just didn't wait for them. But they're still there for the next run.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. Because that regression we had — the one that slipped into production — that was a direct result of someone cutting corners. I don't want to see that again.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Agreed. And honestly, the app stayed healthy after that release, but we got lucky. I'd rather not rely on luck.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Exactly. So from now on, full suite, no skips, no shortcuts. Deal?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Deal. I've learned my lesson. The E2E tests are non-negotiable, and I'll never deploy without running the suite again — even if it takes 20 minutes.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: That's the Mel I know. Coffee's on me.
